To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we cloned two related G protein coupled receptors expressed in lung tissue.

(1) we cloned two novel G protein‐ coupled receptors, GPR12A (also known as GPR4) and GPR6, which are expressed in the human lung and are closely related in sequence; and (2) we determined the tissue expression patterns of GPR12A.
we cloned, sequenced, and characterized a novel G protein‐ coupled receptor, GPR12A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new family of receptors, which are likely to have important functions in inflammatory and other processes in the lung.
the molecular cloning of G‐protein coupled receptors.
the molecular cloning, characterization and tissue distribution of a novel G protein‐linked receptor (GPR6) expressed prominently in the human lung.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two receptors are likely to be receptors for inflammatory mediates.
the two GPCRs are likely to be members of a new receptor family.
GPR6C is a receptor for lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) and GPR12A is a receptor for sphingosylphosphorylcholine (SPC).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have cloned two novel members of the G‐protein coupled receptor super‐family that appear to be expressed in lung tissue.
we have cloned a novel G protein‐linked receptor, GPR12, and identified a related receptor, GPR6, which is identical to GPR4.
we have cloned two new members of the G protein‐couled receptor family that are highly expressed in lung tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the two receptors, GPR12A (also known as GPR6) and GPR6c.1 (also known as C5L2) are very similar and have been found to be expressed in human lung tissue, and that the receptors may be involved in inflammation and/or immunity.
GPR12A may be involved in the regulation of lung inflammation.
we identified a novel receptor that is expressed in the lung and may be involved in the regulation of airway function.
